units.title: Organic molecules and reactions
units.why: Organic chemistry connects carbon structure to fuels, materials and biological molecules.
principles: alkenes contain a carbon-carbon double bond
examples: ethene C₂H₄ can undergo addition polymerisation
methane is an alkane with formula CH₄

videoPackage.title: Carbon structures
videoPackage.transcript: We identify carbon skeletons and functional groups, then connect structure to reactions and material properties.

units.title: Rates and equilibrium
units.why: Reaction rates and equilibrium explain how chemical systems respond to conditions.
principles: effective collisions require sufficient energy and orientation
at equilibrium forward and reverse rates are equal
examples: Powdered solid reacts faster because surface area increases
A catalyst changes rate, not equilibrium position
solutions: both directions continue at equal rates
quizQuestions: What does rate graph slope mean?

videoPackage.title: Chemical systems in motion
videoPackage.transcript: We explain reaction rate with collisions, then show how reversible reactions can settle into dynamic equilibrium.

units.title: Acids, bases and redox
units.why: Acid-base and redox chemistry underpin batteries, biology and environmental processes.
examples: pH 2 is more acidic than pH 4 by factor 100 in [H⁺]

videoPackage.title: Acid-base and electron transfer
videoPackage.transcript: We compare pH logarithmically, identify electron transfer, and keep charge and atoms balanced in redox reasoning.
